summary: The patch correctly generalizes the valid-element count to multiple dims (np.take(mask.shape, axis).prod()), but it folds the array-masking branch under `if hasattr(axis, "__len__")`, so single-dimension reductions (integer axis) no longer hit it and fall through to the scalar `elif` branch — silently breaking per-element min_count masking for the common single-dim case. The correct fix keeps the `if axis is not None and getattr(result, "ndim", False)` gate and only swaps `mask.shape[axis]` for `np.take(mask.shape, axis).prod()`.

issues.description: Regression for single-dim min_count. For an integer axis (e.g. da.sum("dim_0", min_count=2)), `hasattr(axis, "__len__")` is False, so execution skips the array-masking branch and hits `elif`, which only compares the TOTAL valid count (mask.size - mask.sum()) against min_count. Per-column masking is lost: input [[1,nan,3],[nan,nan,6]].sum("dim_0", min_count=2) returns [1,0,9] instead of the correct [nan,nan,9]. Previously this worked via the now-deleted `if axis is not None and getattr(result, "ndim", False)` branch.

Wrong integration of the right idea. np.take(mask.shape, axis).prod() is correct and works for both int and tuple axis, but it was placed under the `hasattr(axis, "__len__")` (tuple/list only) condition. It should replace `mask.shape[axis]` while keeping the original `if axis is not None and getattr(result, "ndim", False)` gate, which covers both single- and multi-dim array results.

Fix is incomplete/asymmetric: it only repairs the multi-dim-to-scalar path shown in the issue while regressing the single-dim-to-array path. The reproduction example da.sum(["dim_0","dim_1"], min_count=1) passes, but the broader min_count contract is no longer honored.
